items.description:

The IHC also issued notices to the police chiefs of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Balochistan, among other officials, seeking their attendance at the next hearing on Sept 10.

items.title: Houthi attacks disrupt Saudi energy facilities, wound 73, authorities say
items.description:
Operations at some energy facilities in Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, were halted on Tuesday following attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels that wounded 73 people, in what Saudi authorities described as a dangerous escalation.
Saudi Arabia’s foreign ministry strongly condemned the “terrorist Houthi militia’s targeting of civilian and economic” sites in the southern cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan, and Najran.
The ministry said the attacks resulted in 73 civilians being injured, including women and children.

items.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect as US trade talks stall
items.description:
Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect just after midnight on Tuesday as Prime Minister Mark Carney increased economic pressure on his country’s biggest trading partner after negotiations collapsed last month, intensifying an 18-month-old trade war.
The counter-tariffs cover $20 billion of US goods, with duties ranging from 15 per cent to 50pc across products from steel and furniture to clothing and electronics.

items.title: The IWT ruling and the coming age of water coercion
items.description:
The Court of Arbitration’s latest ruling on the Indus Waters Treaty deserves attention far beyond Pakistan and India. On August 31, the Court unanimously reaffirmed that the Treaty remains fully in force and rejected the grounds advanced by India for placing it in “abeyance”. It also imposed interim restrictions on specified construction at the Ratle Hydroelectric Plant while the Treaty’s adjudicatory processes continue.
